description: Write the throwaway verification script and run it BEFORE any source change to confirm or refute the lock-hang hypothesis (Gemini summarize_episode running inside LivingUserMemoryService._turn_buffer_lock blocks the chat hot path) and to baseline the OCR behaviour. Must run first. No src/ changes in this feature.
steps: Read plan.md sections 0, 3 and 5 and context.json first.

Create c:\Users\Gtvkun\Documents\GitHub\eris\.agents\tasks\eris-async-summary-no-ocr\verify_async_summary_no_ocr.py per plan section 3: sys.path.insert of the src dir, --phase before|after, --sleep (default 6), temp dirs only, fake adapter with modes ok/fail/hang, checks 1-7, JSON output to results_<phase>.json, 'before' phase never fails the process, 'after' phase exits non-zero on any FAIL. Use hasattr for post-fix APIs (consolidation_status, stop_consolidation, request_consolidation).

Check 1 must time four callables while the fake summarize_episode is sleeping inside dream()/flush_session: LivingUserMemoryService.capture_interpretation_context, TurnMemoryPipeline._enqueue_curator (build as in src/tests/test_memory_interpretation_context.py), LivingUserMemoryService.record_conversation_turn, and StateCommitServiceMixin._ingest_user_turn_memory_hot_path with a SimpleNamespace host and a fake memory_kernel.plan_ingest.

If check 1 shows the hot path blocked for roughly the sleep time, record the measured seconds per callable in findings (hypothesis confirmed). If it does NOT block, find the real blocking lock with thread-stack evidence (sys._current_frames or faulthandler.dump_traceback_later) using the candidate order in plan.md item 1, record it, set status blocked or send_message warning, and do not proceed to FEAT-002 unchanged.

Record in findings: per-callable timings, whether OCR import/force_ocr happened (check 5), the false-positive route table for the 3 real sentences with OCR on and off (check 6, report only), and the rollup ValueError probe results (check 7).
acceptance_criteria: verify_async_summary_no_ocr.py exists in the task dir and runs with --phase before without crashing (exit code 0).
results_before.json exists and contains timings for all four hot-path callables and a verdict for checks 1-7.
findings states explicitly whether the _turn_buffer_lock hypothesis is confirmed or refuted, with measured numbers.
No file under src/ was modified.
verification: c:\Users\Gtvkun\Documents\GitHub\eris\.venv\Scripts\python.exe c:\Users\Gtvkun\Documents\GitHub\eris\.agents\tasks\eris-async-summary-no-ocr\verify_async_summary_no_ocr.py --phase before ; then confirm results_before.json exists and git status shows no change under src/
findings:
HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED (fake Gemini summarize_episode sleeps 6.0 s, run via LivingUserMemoryService.dream() which flushes inline). Script: .agents/tasks/eris-async-summary-no-ocr/verify_async_summary_no_ocr.py; output results_before.json (total 43 s, exit 0). Each callable ran on its own fresh scenario, started once the adapter was mid-call.

CHECK 1 (FAIL, expected): hot-path callables blocked for ~the whole sleep: capture_interpretation_context 5.661 s; TurnMemoryPipeline._enqueue_curator 6.012 s; record_conversation_turn 6.003 s; StateCommitServiceMixin._ingest_user_turn_memory_hot_path 6.017 s (limit 1.0 s). Thread-stack evidence: the background thread sits in service.py flush_session -> _flush_buffer_locked -> consolidate_session -> episode_builder.build -> _from_model -> summarize_episode (holding _turn_buffer_lock). The probe threads wait at service.py:232 capture_interpretation_context (`with self._turn_buffer_lock`) and service.py:165 record_conversation_turn (`with self._turn_buffer_lock`); the ingest hot path blocks via enqueue_user_turn -> _enqueue_curator -> capture_interpretation_context. No other lock needs to be involved.

CHECK 2 (PASS at baseline, nuance): late turns are not lost, but the first late record_conversation_turn blocked 6.013 s (then 0.025 s, 0.011 s); after the call the buffer holds late1..late3 only, the episode is persisted (source episode_model), and a fresh service reloaded from disk sees both. So the baseline problem is latency of the hot path, not data loss, for the ok path.

CHECK 3 (FAIL, expected): (i) with a failing adapter (CuratorInferenceError provider_error) dream() writes a heuristic episode (source=episode_fallback, summary 'Nguoi dung tap trung vao: ...') and clears the buffer (buffer_len 0), no retry state exists (no consolidation_status API). Confirms plan section 0: a Gemini failure silently replaces the real summary with a crude one. (ii) hang+timeout, (iii) single-flight, (iv) user-turn gate are N/A at baseline (request_consolidation absent; hang would hold the lock 30 s).

CHECK 4 (FAIL, expected): capture_interpretation_context during the summary blocked 6.01 s (with older episode) and 6.023 s (without); episode_prompt_view does not take the lock and returned in 0.006-0.010 s. While blocked, the buffer is not readable, so chat gets neither the older episode nor raw recent turns until the call ends (after it ends the new episode is visible and recent_conversation is empty because the buffer was cleared).

CHECK 5 (FAIL, expected) with ERIS_SCREEN_OCR_ENABLED unset: IncrementalScreenTextWorker.start() constructs both OCR backends (rapidocr, pytesseract); import attempts recorded for rapidocr_onnxruntime and pytesseract (numpy is installed in the dev .venv, so the rapidocr import is reached; onnxruntime is not reached because rapidocr_onnxruntime itself is missing); the self-heal runs `python -m pip --version` and `python -m pip install ... rapidocr-onnxruntime>=1.3.24,<2` (subprocess.run was faked, nothing was installed); worker.backend is a placeholder _OCRBackend named 'none', not None; snapshots already report backend='uia_only' because the dev venv has no OCR packages. prepare_turn('nhin man hinh di') (explicit, not inherited) -> route mode=vision needs_visual=False reason=no_usable_screen_text_escalate_vision, refresh_now(force_ocr=True) is called, capture_fn is NOT called this turn and pending_vision is queued (vision delayed a turn); same for 'tu xem di'. With ERIS_SCREEN_OCR_ENABLED=1 and a fake backend the old OCR path works (switch_on_restores_old_path PASS, force_ocr=True passed), which FEAT-003 must keep working.

CHECK 6 (REPORT only, identical with OCR on and off at baseline because the env var is ignored): with the 3 real sentences after the real preceding Eris turns (containing 'anh' / 'code'): 'vụ đó lâu rồi á', 'nó ko hiểu ý tôi. làm ko hợp ý', 'cái này ko hay. tôi tâm sự cái này còn hỏi lại kỹ thuật, fe tệ quá nha' each give references_screen=True, inherited=True, mode=vision, needs_visual=False, route reason anaphora_without_screen_text_escalate_vision, refresh_now(force_ocr=True) called, capture not called this turn, pending_vision queued. This reproduces the false positive (P2) in the router. Fix suggestion unchanged: stop matching accent-folded 'anh'/'code' anchors and 'no'/'do'/'day' deictics in screen_anaphora_rescue.py, match the accented original ('ảnh').

CHECK 7 (PASS): EpisodeRollupStore.run returns {status: failed, error: ValueError, reason: ''} with no detail for anchor-not-allowed, 9 segments and duplicate anchors (case a-c: 1 adapter call each). Correction to plan section 5: a corrupt rollup JSON yields error 'JSONDecodeError' (subclass of ValueError, but type(exc).__name__ prints the subclass), 0 adapter calls; a plain 'ValueError' therefore comes from _validate or invalid_episode_rollup_store, not from a corrupt-JSON read. Control (valid response) committed. Detail field is absent, as expected before the item-2 change.

Script notes for later phases: sleeps use Event.wait so cleanup can release the fake adapter early; cache path ERIS_LIGHT_OCR_CACHE_PATH, subprocess.run and OCR backends are patched/restored inside check 5; AFTER-only sub-checks (3ii-iv) call request_consolidation/consolidation_status/stop_consolidation via hasattr and the gate check patches the class attribute InferenceBroker.user_turn_active, so FEAT-002 must read the gate from GLOBAL_INFERENCE_BROKER.user_turn_active() at run time and expose consolidation_status() keys: pending, failures, next_retry_in_s, last_error (string containing 'timeout' for a timeout). Nothing under src/ was modified; git status shows only the pre-existing user changes plus the untracked task dirs.
